records.finding: [review round 1] The pushed-down SQL predicates were inert in every test: the fake served every fixture row regardless, so all eight payloadPaths JSONPaths were never compared, and a drifted path would return zero rows against real BigQuery with the suite green. The engine reports that zero as a deterministic realized/customer-impact figure.
records.evidence: The fake now interprets and EVALUATES the emitted statement (planStatement/matchesPlan), failing loudly on any clause it cannot evaluate; conformance queries filter on every label; the suite runs both a pushdown-honouring and a pushdown-ignoring backend. Verified by mutating each of the eight paths to a different key the exporter does write — all eight now die in the conformance suite.

records.finding: [review round 1] time.Format truncates, so a Range.To with a sub-microsecond tail bound the microsecond BELOW it. An entry at exactly that microsecond is inside memq's half-open [From, To) and outside the fetch, and memq cannot re-admit a row the query never returned — so the pushdown stopped being a superset of the window it claims to widen.
records.evidence: lowerBoundParam truncates (widening) and upperBoundParam applies ceilMicro (widening). TestWindowBoundsStayASuperset pins all four rendering directions; TestSubMicrosecondWindowKeepsTheBoundaryEvent pins the behaviour. Both mutation directions die.

records.finding: [review round 1] The BigQuery server-side wait and the default client deadline were both 30s, so the jobComplete:false answer could not arrive before the client gave up: the polling loop was unreachable with the adapter's own default doer, and a slow query surfaced as a transport timeout instead of a poll.
records.evidence: Split into serverWait (20s, what goes on the wire) and defaultHTTPTimeout (60s, the constructor's client). TestServerWaitFitsInsideTheClientDeadline pins the ordering, a 10s minimum margin, and that the request body carries serverWait.

records.finding: [review round 2] The residual of the round-1 pushdown finding. The only query filtering on the stage label filtered on "capture", which the api-5xx fixture never emits, so that comparison was empty-vs-empty and $."biz.stage" was still free to drift to any other key the exporter writes. The round-1 mutation suite reported it killed only because it mutated to an ABSENT key, which the drift fence catches on shape alone.
records.evidence: Reproduced by hand before fixing. The stage query now filters "settle", which the fixture emits 209 of in-window. The conformance loop records a per-label WITNESS — a query filtering on that label whose ORACLE answer is non-empty — and fails any label without one; that replaces TestPushdownCoversEveryLabel, which only checked a label was MENTIONED. A third mutation pass now swaps each path for a different key the exporter does write, bypassing the drift fence.

records.finding: [review round 2] The marker check was a full unmarshal, so any payload that is not a JSON object was classed as foreign and skipped. Reachable through WithView pointed at a table whose payload column is STRING rather than JSON: TO_JSON_STRING then yields a JSON string literal, every row is skipped, and the read answers an empty window with no error — a measured zero on a money leg.
records.evidence: outcomeMarker now separates 'not ours' from 'not decodable'. A single non-object row is still skipped (a text log line is genuinely foreign), but a result set in which NOT ONE row is an object is refused with an error naming the column. TestWrongPayloadColumnIsLoud covers both sides, including that one real object among noise is a normal mixed log stream and that zero rows is an empty window, not a column error.

records.evidence: New refuses a non-positive interval; the doc comment moved with the behaviour; two rows added to the validation table.

records.finding: [review round 3] The fake's own interpreter stored predicates in a map keyed by the extracted JSON key, so two labels resolving to one JSONPath silently dropped one predicate — the exact behaviour its doc comment promised never happens. Real BigQuery answers two contradictory equalities on one key with zero rows; the fake served the rows the dropped predicate should have excluded. This left the kind label's path unverified even after the round-2 witness, because kind's only witness query also filters on segment.
records.evidence: plan.filters is a slice of (key, value) pairs, so every predicate is evaluated, and planStatement fails loudly when one key is bound to two different values. Verified: kind, segment and currency each remapped onto a colliding path now die in the conformance suite.

records.finding: [review round 3] The row cap and the paging loop were never exercised together — truncation only ever inside one page — so the loop's own bound was unasserted: changing len(all) <= maxRows to < returned a truncated window as a smaller number with no error.
records.evidence: TestTruncationIsLoud is now a six-row table crossing page boundaries in both directions and asserts the untruncated total, not only the error. TestPagingFailuresAreLoud and TestPollAndPageURLsCarryTheLocation cover three further defensive branches the examiner reported untested: a repeated page token, a job going incomplete mid-paging, and the location parameter on the getQueryResults URL.

records.finding: [review round 3] MaxResults not being maxRows+1 survives every test.
records.evidence: Equivalent mutant, not a defect: MaxResults is a per-page hint, and the statement's LIMIT maxRows+1 is the truncation sentinel that bounds the total. A test for it would assert nothing. The field now carries a comment saying so, because reading it as the money-safety mechanism is what made it look like a defect.
